If you challenge directly, but it doesn't feel like you care deeply, you're just an asshole and they're just like, yeah, God, you get really defensive. I should get her on this podcast. How cool would that be?
turns.zh: 对，它讲的就是。我想再强调你刚说的：核心是，当你想给别人直接反馈时，你要让它清楚地表明你深深关心他们。我喜欢她聊到的：如果你把其中一条做错了，会发生什么。如果你直接挑战、但不让人觉得你深深关心，你就只是个 asshole，对方就「对，天呐」，变得极度防御。我应该把她请上这个播客。那得多酷啊？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Oh my God, that would be my, she's my... If I could meet one tech celebrity, it would be her.
turns.zh: 我的天，那会是我……她是我的……如果我能见一位科技名人，那就是她。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. I'm going to work on it. If you're listening and you're Kim Scott, let me know, I will try to get to her. Anything else in that bucket of frameworks or tools, things that you find really helpful leadership?
turns.zh: 好。我去努力。如果你在听，而且你是 Kim Scott，跟我讲一声，我去试着请她。那个领导力的框架/工具桶里，还有别的什么你觉得特别有帮助的吗？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: The only other one, I'm not a huge framework person. I think this goes back to my gut thing, but the one other thing that I refer to often is I love the Eisenhower Matrix, which is also known as the four Ds. So it's do, defer, delegate, delete, you have also quadrants. Maybe my brain just works in quadrants. I don't know. But I totally subscribe to that and that's how I do everything, where I write everything down at the end of every day, I go through and I either do delegate, defer, delete, and it really helps you clear a lot of stuff out of your brain.
turns.zh: 另一个，我也不是个框架狂人。我觉得这又回到我那个「凭直觉」的事上了。但我常引用的另一件是，我爱艾森豪威尔矩阵（Eisenhower Matrix），也叫四个 D：Do（做）、Defer（推迟）、Delegate（委派）、Delete（删掉），你也有象限。也许我的大脑就是按象限工作的，不知道。但我完全认同它，我什么事都这么干：每天结束我把所有事写下来，过一遍，要么做、委派、推迟、删掉——它真的帮你把一堆东西从脑子里清出去。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Interesting. So you don't even use it as a grid necessarily, it's more make a decision on all the things on your plate?
turns.zh: 有意思。所以你甚至不一定要把它当 grid 用，更多是对手头所有事做个决定？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yeah, I do. I just tried using the grid view and it didn't work for me for some reason. So I just use a to-do list, and then I don't let myself finish working until I've gone through anything I didn't get through that day, and then I know what I have to do the next day.
turns.zh: 对，是的。我试过用 grid 视图，但不知为何对我没用。所以我就是用一个 to-do list，然后我不让自己在下班前不把当天没做完的事过一遍，这样我就知道第二天要做什么。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So that touches on another area I wanted to touch on, which is productivity. I hear you're very good at being productive and making the use of your time. I guess one, where do you think that comes from? And then two, just any other tips, tactics, tools you find to be really effective in staying productive?
turns.zh: 这又带出我想聊的另一个领域：生产力。我听说你特别擅长高效、善用时间。我想一问，你觉得这来自哪里？二问，还有什么其他你觉得在保持高效上特别有效的技巧、战术、工具？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yeah, where does that come from? I think I am OCD. I think I'm an overachiever. I don't know, it's really important to me. I think when my team says that I'm very productive, the feedback I hear from them is they're impressed that they send me a doc and then I always read it. I think that's more about prioritizing my team and making sure that they're unblocked, which I take very seriously. I don't know other tips that I would give people. I write everything down because I think I'm one of those people I remember things best when they're written down and then I obsessively put things on my to-do list. Anything that anyone asks me to do goes on there, and then I have that method for organizing it later in the day.
turns.zh: 对，这来自哪里？我想我有 OCD。我觉得我是个 overachiever。不知道，这对我很重要。团队说我很高效时，我从他们那儿听到的反馈是：他们惊讶于他们发我一个 doc，我总是会读。我想那更多是关于把团队优先级放前面、确保他们不被卡住——这一点我看得极重。别的小贴士我也不知道能给什么。我把所有事都写下来，因为我是那种写下来才记得最牢的人，然后我会强迫症式地把事情丢进我的 to-do list。任何人让我做的事都进那个 list，然后我用那个方法在当天晚些时候整理它。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have an app for this or do you write it on paper?
turns.zh: 你是用 app 还是写在纸上？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: I use Todoist. I think you can use any, but it's the one that works best for me. I love using paper, but then if I don't have it with me, then I can't remember anything I have to do, so I've had to go digital.
turns.zh: 我用 Todoist。我想你用哪个都行，但它是对我最好用的。我超爱用纸，但如果我没带纸在身上，我就记不住任何要做的事，所以我不得不数字化。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. So it sounds like a big part of your process is just getting things out of your head and writing it down somewhere.
turns.zh: 太棒了。所以听起来你流程的一大块就是把东西从脑子里搬出来、写到某个地方。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yes. I think that's huge. And I also think if you're in any sort of job, I think most PMs have this where it's so much of your job is actually deep thinking and problem solving. I just cannot get that done if I'm running through my to-do list in my head. So I think that was a big unlock for me when I realized that I just needed to, anytime I'm stressed, honestly, if I just sit and make a list of all the things I have to do, I'm like, oh, it's four things, I can get those done, it's okay.
turns.zh: 是的。我觉得那超级重要。而且我想，只要你做的是任何这类工作——我觉得大部分 PM 都是这样——你工作里的很大一部分其实是深度思考和解决问题。如果我脑子里一直跑着 to-do list，我根本没法完成那个。所以当我意识到「只要一有压力，就坐下来把所有要做的事列个单子」，那对我是个大解锁——我会想，哦，就四件事，我能做完，没事。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Man, that tool of just making a list when you're stressed about, all the things you got to do, just making a list of it on paper, I find it so helpful.
turns.zh: 老兄，那种「有压力、有一堆事要做时，就把它在纸上列个单子」的工具，我觉得太有帮助了。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: It works every time.
turns.zh: 每次都管用。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Have you read Getting Things Done by David Allen?
turns.zh: 你读过 David Allen 的《Getting Things Done》（搞定）吗？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: It's on my list. I haven't read it.
turns.zh: 在我 list 上。我还没读。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. That book totally transformed how I think about productivity, and you already doing a lot of what he recommends. It's like this very old book. And now he's just, I don't know, he's a public speaker dude that just goes around consulting. But this one, it has very simple approaches to being productive and it really changed the way I operate. And you're already doing a lot of it, so I don't know how much value you get out of it.
turns.zh: 好。那本书彻底改变了我对生产力的看法，而且你已经做了很多他建议的事。那是本很老的书。现在他就只是……不知道，一个到处做咨询的演讲者。但这本里有特别朴素的可行方法，真的改变了我的运作方式。而且你已经做了很多了，所以我不知道你能从中获得多少价值。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: I'll read it. I love this stuff.
turns.zh: 我会读的。我爱这类东西。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: A core concept is this idea of mind like water where you don't want to have anything in your head, you want to get it all out. And then there's these systems for how to process all the things you're getting out.
turns.zh: 一个核心概念是「mind like water（心如止水）」这个想法——你不想脑子里塞任何东西，你想把它全倒出来。然后还有一些系统，用来处理你倒出来的所有这些东西。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Totally.
turns.zh: 完全同意。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Maybe we'll get David Allen this. We got a whole list.
turns.zh: 也许我们能把这个 David Allen 也请来。我们有一整个 list 了。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: I know we have a whole hit list.
turns.zh: 我知道，我们有整整一个 hit list。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Maybe it's just a final question. You're good at so many things, another thing you're really good at is public speaking. I was watching the last Spotify launch event and I was just like, holy moly, she's incredibly good at speaking and it's something I want to get better at and something I think a 100% of people want to get better at. So, I'm just curious, what have you learned about being an effective public speaker? Anything that you could recommend to people if they're trying to get better at this?
turns.zh: 也许这当最后一个问题。你这么多事都做得好，另一件你特别在行的是公开演讲。我看上次 Spotify 发布会，就在想，我的天，她演讲厉害得离谱，而这是我想变得更好的事，也是我觉得 100% 的人都想变得更好的事。所以我只是好奇，关于做一个有效的公开演讲者，你学到了什么？如果别人想在这上面变好，你能给什么建议？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Well, first of all, thank you for saying I'm awesome at so many things. This is my favorite podcast I've ever been on, you're just complimenting me the whole time, so I'll take it.
turns.zh: 首先，谢谢你夸我这么多事都牛。这是我上过最爱的播客了，你整场都在夸我，那我就收下了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: True.
turns.zh: 真的。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: I think with public speaking, for me, the first thing that I had to do was decide that I didn't hate public speaking because I think it's human nature. It makes sense that we do not want to be in front of a crowd and we don't want to be performing. And it's just an unnatural thing that humans, I think make ourselves do. I remember actually when I was in high school, I had to give a presentation and I had so much anxiety I couldn't sleep the night before. And I remember I was getting ready for school that morning and I was like, I'm just not going to hate public speaking. I just can't get through my life feeling this way. And so I just got up there and I had fun with it, and it felt so much better to not feel worried about it.
turns.zh: 我觉得关于公开演讲，对我来说，第一件我得做的事，是决定自己「不讨厌公开演讲」。因为我想那是人性，我们不想站在人群面前、不想表演，这很合理。那只是人类让自己去做的一件不自然的事。我记得高中时，我有次要做一个展示，焦虑到前一晚睡不着。早上我准备去上学时想，我就是不打算讨厌公开演讲。我没法带着这种感觉过我的人生。于是我就站上去、玩得开心，而那种不担心它的感觉好太多了。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: So I think ever since then I've been okay at it. And then I have gotten lots of opportunities to do big scary public speaking things for Spotify, and so I think I've had to get even better. I think my tips would be my biggest one is probably reframing. Everyone has this anxiety before they have to perform or they go on stage. Reframing that anxiety to understand that the thing your body is doing is surging you with adrenaline to help you. And so letting that feeling wash over you instead of fighting it, I think has been so effective for me because otherwise, it can feel like a panic attack. And so I think you have to be like, cool, my body's getting ready. We're excited, we're going to go do this on stage. That has been really helpful. I practice a million times anytime I have to do public speaking.
turns.zh: 所以我想从那以后我就还行了。然后我有了很多为 Spotify 做那种又大又吓人的公开演讲的机会，所以我想我不得不变得更好。我的建议里，最大的一条大概是「reframing（重新框定）」。每个人在上台表演前都有这种焦虑。把那种焦虑重新框定为：你身体正在做的事，是在往你身上灌肾上腺素来帮你。所以让那种感觉冲刷过你、而不是跟它对抗，我想这对我特别有效——否则它会像恐慌发作。所以我想你得这样：酷，我的身体在准备了。我们很兴奋，我们要上台去做这件事了。这帮了大忙。任何一次公开演讲，我都会练习一百万遍。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: So I think everybody has different memorization tactics, different ways of doing speaker notes that work for them. And so I think part of it is you have to do a bunch of public speaking to see what works for you. So some people work best with no notes. I almost read complete sentences a good, I can enunciate things while I'm reading, so that works best for me. Some people like bullets and then they go a little bit off the script. But I think once you figure out what method of speaker notes works for you, I rehearse probably at least 10 times all the way through once the speaker notes are final. And you can practice your exact delivery. You can practice where you're going to put jokes in. You can figure out what doesn't feel natural or where you're going to trip it up, and then you can change the words that you're using.
turns.zh: 所以我想每个人有不同的记忆战术、不同的 speaker notes（演讲提示）用法。一部分是你得做够多次公开演讲，才能看出什么对你 work。有些人最好什么都不带；我几乎是把完整句子读出来——我能边读边把字咬清楚，所以那对我最好用。有些人喜欢要点、然后稍微脱稿。但我想一旦你搞清楚哪种 speaker notes 方式适合你，在 notes 定稿后，我会把整场至少排练 10 遍。你能练习你准确的表达；你能练把笑话放在哪儿；你能发现哪里不自然、哪里会卡，然后改掉你用的词。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: And so I like to get to the point where I can remember ad-lib at least half of the notes that I have in there, and that way I know I'm going to feel confident coming off script. I make a lot of eye contact with the audience, which I think makes them think that I'm not reading speaker notes. So I think that's really important. If you can stand it, which I can't, record yourself or watch yourself in a mirror, it messes me up more. But I think for a lot of people, that can be really helpful to figure out where your issues are. I think the biggest thing for me honestly, is that the unfair advantage I have is if you really give a shit about what you're talking about, you are going to be such a better presenter because people are going to be able to tell that you care.
turns.zh: 所以我喜欢练到至少能即兴说出 notes 里一半的内容，这样我就知道自己脱稿时会有信心。我跟观众有大量眼神接触，我想那让他们以为我没在读 speaker notes。所以我觉得那真的重要。如果你受得了（我受不了），把自己录下来、或者对着镜子看——那会让我更乱。但我想对很多人来说，那能帮你发现你的问题在哪儿。对我而言最大的事，老实说是：我那不公平的 advantage 是——如果你真的在乎你在讲的东西，你会是个好太多的演讲者，因为大家能看出你在乎。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: And so I think even at a larger Spotify event where it's like I'm reading off a teleprompter and I'm reading, I'm marketing, but I'm helping write those words and then the way that I'm saying them matters because I'm talking to podcasters and I'm like, my mission in life is to make things better for you, not everyone gets that benefit, I guess. Sometimes you have to do public speaking about things that you're not very passionate about, but I certainly think that helps. And I think leaning into that, so when you can, telling personal stories, letting the audience get to know you, I like to work some humor into my presentations. I think that can really help as well.
turns.zh: 所以我想哪怕在一个更大的 Spotify 活动上，我是在读提词器、在做 marketing，但那些词是我帮忙写的，而我怎么说它们很重要——因为我是跟播客主在对话，而我在想「我人生的使命就是让你们的事更好」，不是所有人都有这个好处，我猜。有时候你不得不讲一些你没那么 passion 的事，但我肯定觉得那有帮助。而且我想 lean into 这点：所以只要能，就讲个人故事、让观众了解你。我喜欢在我的演讲里加点幽默。我想那也真能帮上忙。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That is awesome advice. I especially love letting the stress wash over you, because most of has this challenge. Your body's just doing all this shit that's just going to stress the shit out of you. And so the idea of just embracing it, just flowing with it.
turns.zh: 那建议太棒了。我特别爱「让压力冲刷过你」这点，因为大部分人都有这个挑战。你的身体就在干那一堆 shit，只会把你 stress 到爆。所以「拥抱它、随它流动」这个想法——

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yes, it's a superpower. It's like, that's so cool, that adrenaline works that way.
turns.zh: 对，那是个 superpower。就像，太酷了，肾上腺素是那样运作的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. Okay. I'm going to try that one.
turns.zh: 对。好。我要试试那个。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Also, if you're nervous, you can put your hands above your head that'll help the blood, I don't know, it helps it go into your head or something. I don't remember.
turns.zh: 还有，如果你紧张，你可以把手举过头顶，那会帮助血液——我不知道——帮它进到脑子里还是什么的。我不记得了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's this whole power post thing that apparently has-
turns.zh: 有个整套「power pose（力量姿势）」的东西，显然已经——

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yes, exactly.
turns.zh: 对，没错。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I think it's been disproven. People are like, no, there's no data that shows that. But the blood thing that's really interesting versus psychological benefits.
turns.zh: 我想那已经被证伪了。大家说，不，没有数据显示那个。但血液那个真的很意思，跟心理益处相对。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: I think there is a real physiological thing that happens.
turns.zh: 我想确实有个真实的生理反应在发生。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's cool. Okay. Amazing. Okay. Maybe as an actual last question, what's happening in the future of the Spotify podcasting platform? Anything you want to share about where things are going?
turns.zh: 那挺酷。好。太棒了。好。也许作为真正的最后一个问题：Spotify 播客平台的未来会怎样？关于走向，有什么想分享的？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: A lot of the things that I talked about at Stream on for anyone who saw that this year, I think are still very much our strategy. So I think for us in general, Spotify is really focused on making sure that we can... We have a massive audience, we have more than 500 million monthly active listeners. We want to help podcast creators reach that global audience, and so it's really important to us. I always tell my team the biggest problem that I want to solve for podcasters is discovery and audience growth, and I really think we can be the ones to do it, so I'm really excited about that. So discovery, monetization. We're really focused on making sure that creators of all shapes and sizes can make a living off of their work.
turns.zh: 我在今年 Stream On 上聊的很多事，看过的 anyone，我想依然非常是我们战略的一部分。所以总体上，Spotify 真的专注于确保我们能……我们有庞大的受众，月度活跃听众超 5 亿。我们想帮播客创作者触达那个全球受众，所以这对我们非常重要。我总跟团队说，我想为播客主解决的最大问题是「发现」和「受众增长」，而我真的觉得我们能成为做成这件事的人，所以我对那个超兴奋。所以：发现、变现。我们真的专注于确保各种规模、各种类型的创作者都能靠自己的作品谋生。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: And then I think in general, we're working on so many cool things at Spotify to make podcasts a more interactive format, something that allows you to get to know your audience and connect with your fan base. We talked about a couple features this past year. I definitely can't say anything specific, but what I can say is there is lots of really cool stuff coming next year that I'm very excited about. And I would say for anyone who wants to learn more, definitely sign up for Spotify for podcasters. It works whether you're hosted with Spotify or not, and you can start to get a sense of some of those features that we're opening up to everybody, but there's lots more cool stuff to come.
turns.zh: 然后总体上，我们在 Spotify 做着好多超酷的事，让播客成为一种更互动的形式，一种让你能了解受众、跟你的粉丝群连接的东西。我们今年聊过几个功能。我肯定不能说具体的，但我能说的是，明年会有很多超酷的东西，我特别兴奋。而对任何想多了解的人，绝对去注册 Spotify for Podcasters。不管你是不是托管在 Spotify 都 work，你能开始感受到我们向所有人开放的一些功能，但还有更多酷东西要来。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing, mysterious, and exciting. With that, we've reached our very exciting lightning round. Are you ready?
turns.zh: 太棒了，神秘又让人兴奋。说到这，我们到了超级刺激的闪电轮环节。准备好了吗？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 好了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What are two or three books that you recommend most to other people?
turns.zh: 你会最推荐给别人的两三本书是什么？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Children of Time, and I guess I would say It by Stephen King. I recommend a lot of Stephen King books, but that's my all time favorite.
turns.zh: 《Children of Time》（时间之子），然后我想我会说 Stephen King 的《It》（它）。我推荐过很多 Stephen King 的书，但那是我有史以来最爱的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Very on brand with your podcasts. Makes sense. What is a recent movie or TV show that you've really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 跟你播客的调性很搭。说得通。你最近真的很喜欢的一部电影或剧集是什么？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: TV show, I'll just say, I guess Pokerface was the last one that really blew my mind. Movies, I mean, Barbie was so good, and then I'll just give you a lesser known one. I just watched this crazy movie from the '80s that was made the same year Home Alone was, this just got featured on a podcast, so I think everybody's talking about it now, but it's a horror movie about a kid who's home alone, and then he has to fight Santa Claus in a home invasion situation. It is so good, it has a bunch of different names, but if you look up either Game Over or it's like Code Père Noël or something, it's an old French horror movie, so good.
turns.zh: 剧集，我就说——我想《Poker Face》（扑克脸）是最后一部真让我 mind-blown 的。电影嘛，《Barbie》（芭比）就很好，然后我给你一个不太出名的：我刚看了这部 80 年代的疯电影，跟《Home Alone》（小鬼当家）同年拍的——这刚在某个播客上被 featured，所以我想现在大家都在聊它了——但它是部关于一个小孩独自在家、然后得在一场 home invasion 里对抗圣诞老人的恐怖片。太好看了，它有一堆不同的名字，但如果你搜「Game Over」或者「Code Père Noël」之类的，它是部老法国恐怖片，超好看。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Interesting that the other Home Alone is the one that did well in this one.
turns.zh: 有意思，另一部《Home Alone》是那部卖得好的，而这部没有。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Well, there was apparently a whole legal thing over it.
turns.zh: 对，显然为这个有过一整场法律纠纷。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh, wow. They didn't have Macaulay Culkin. That's their missing piece. What is a favorite interview question that you'd like to ask candidates when you're interviewing?
turns.zh: 哦，哇。他们没有 Macaulay Culkin。那是他们缺的那块拼图。你面试时最喜欢问候选人什么问题？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: I have one. It is, if you could make a podcast about anything, what would it be? And it is the best. Honestly, you should ask people that even if you don't work in work in podcasting, because it tells you so much about candidates, and one thing that I feel very strongly is that the most important thing is that you're hiring passionate people, not people who are passionate necessarily about the thing that you're doing, but about anything. If they can't think of anything, that's a red flag for me.
turns.zh: 我有一个。是：「如果你可以做一期关于任何事的播客，那会是什么？」这个最棒了。老实说，就算你不在播客行业工作，你也该问人这个，因为它能告诉你关于候选人太多东西了。而我一个感觉特别强烈的点是：最重要的事是你招的是有 passion 的人，不一定是 passion 于你正在做的这件事，而是 passion 于任何事。如果他们什么都想不出来，那对我来说是个 red flag。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's awesome. It's like a variation of the question of Teach me something or tell me about something that you've learned recently. Really interesting tweak on that question and very appropriate. What is a favorite product or something awesome you've discovered recently that you really like digital or physical?
turns.zh: 那太棒了。就像是「教我点东西」或者「告诉我你最近学到了什么」的变体。对那个问题的一种很有意思的 tweak，而且非常贴切。你最近发现的一个最喜欢的产品、或者某个你真的很喜欢的东西，数字或实体都行？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Okay. Very unsexy answer, but I love 1-800-CONTACTS.
turns.zh: 好。很 unsexy 的答案，但我爱 1-800-CONTACTS。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: I'm so impressed with their product team. If you need new contacts, even if you need a new prescription, you can do the whole thing online in five minutes, and it's so well-thought-out and so thoughtful. I love them. And then the one other one I'll give a shout-out to, since becoming a parent, Love Every, do you subscribe to them?
turns.zh: 我对他们的产品团队印象极深。如果你需要新的隐形眼镜，哪怕需要新的处方，你可以在线上五分钟搞定整个流程，而且设计得那么周全、那么体贴。我爱他们。另一个我要 shout-out 的，是自从当了父母后发现的 Love Every，你订他们家吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Absolutely. I don't know anyone that doesn't have them.
turns.zh: 当然。我不认识任何没订他们家的人。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: I know. It's so good.
turns.zh: 我知道。太好了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: They've cracked it.
turns.zh: 他们破局了。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. We are missing some of the toys, and so we're trying to find where they went because he's ready for the rattle.
turns.zh: 对。我们缺了几个玩具，所以我们在找它们去哪儿了，因为他已经准备好玩摇铃了。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yes. Awesome.
turns.zh: 对。太棒了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. I love everybody's amazing and their ads are really great. Oh, man.
turns.zh: 对。我爱大家，他们家太厉害了，而且他们的广告真的很好。哦天呐。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yes. They're so good.
turns.zh: 对。他们太好了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What is a favorite life motto that you come back to often share with folks? Anything there?
turns.zh: 你最常回到的、会分享给他人的一句人生格言是什么？有吗？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: "Only a fool wishes time away." Even if you're having a bad day, even if you're doing something boring or you're stressed, you have to do public speaking, that's still your life and you should enjoy it.
turns.zh: 「Only a fool wishes time away.（只有傻子才愿时光飞逝。）」哪怕你今天过得很糟、哪怕你在做无聊的事、或者你压力大得非得去公开演讲，那依然是你的人生，你应该享受它。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that. There's this phrase of just like, I'm just killing time right now, and I always think about that, just like, oh, but you don't have that much time. Maybe you shouldn't try to kill yourself.
turns.zh: 我爱那句。有句话大概是说「我只是在杀时间」，我总想到那个——就「哦，但你时间没那么多。也许你不该试着杀你自己」。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Even though sometimes things are boring, it reminds me of another quote of just, "Most of the world's problems are caused by our inability to sit in a room for 10 minutes quietly."
turns.zh: 哪怕有时候事情很无聊，这让我想起另一句引语：「世上大部分的问题，都源于我们无法安静地在一间屋里坐上十分钟。」

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yes. Also, if you're bored, have a baby because you'll never be bored again.
turns.zh: 对。还有，如果你无聊，去生个娃，因为你再也不会无聊了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. Yep, indeed. Speaking of parenting, what is a valuable lesson that your mom or your dad taught you?
turns.zh: 对。是啊，确实。说到当父母，你爸妈教过你什么宝贵的功课？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: My mom always told me that my generosity would be rewarded, so anytime that I was nice or thought of someone else before me, she always made sure that I got some little reward or got to go out for ice cream or something, I think that really worked on me.
turns.zh: 我妈总跟我说，我的慷慨会有回报。所以任何时候我表现好、或者先想到别人再想到自己，她总会确保我得到点小奖励、或者能出去吃个冰淇淋什么的。我想那真的对我起作用了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that. Final question, I saw somewhere that you raised bait backyard chickens. Is that true?
turns.zh: 我爱那个。最后一个问题，我在哪儿看到说你养了后院的鸡（backyard chickens）。是真的吗？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: I'm so happy you asked about my chickens'.
turns.zh: 我太开心你问我的鸡了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that reaction. So maybe just why did you decide to do that and any tips for someone that may want to explore it?
turns.zh: 我爱这个反应。所以也许就聊聊：你为什么决定养？还有给想尝试的人什么 tips？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Oh my God. Well, we should have started with this because I can talk about this for an hour and a half, but I love my chickens. I have eight of them, we've got one rooster and seven hens. I think that all of us should be a little bit closer to nature, to the, I was going to say, the food that we're eating, I'm not going to eat my chickens, but they make eggs for me. But I just think there is something very lacking in our modern lives, that connection to nature. When I feel stressed at work and I go outside and I hang out with my chickens, I pet them, and I give them treats and we talk to each other. It's like nothing makes me happier and feel more grounded than hanging out with my chickens. So I think everyone should have chickens. I would say they're pretty low maintenance, so if you're thinking about it, I would recommend it. And if you get chickens, my favorite thing that I did for them, I got this monthly subscription box for chickens I think it's called Coop Crate.
turns.zh: 我的天。嗯，我们应该从这就开始聊，因为我能讲这个讲一个半小时，但我爱我的鸡。我有八只，一只公鸡、七只母鸡。我想我们所有人都该离自然、离——我本来想说离我们吃的食物——近一点；我不会吃我的鸡，但它们给我下蛋。但我就觉得我们的现代生活缺了某种东西，那种与自然的连接。当我在工作中感到压力，去外面跟我的鸡待着，我摸摸它们、给它们零食、我们互相说话。没有什么比跟我的鸡待着更让我开心、更让我踏实了。所以我想每个人都该养鸡。我会说它们挺低维护的，所以如果你在考虑，我推荐。而且如果你养鸡，我给它们做的最爱的一件事是：我订了一个给鸡的月度订阅盒，我想叫 Coop Crate。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Love Every for Chickens.
turns.zh: 给鸡的 Love Every。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Yes, it's Love Every for Chickens and every month they send me chicken treats, but also fun little things for crazy chicken people, so it's clothes or a sticker, something funny.I'm very into the whole chicken thing, so, yeah.
turns.zh: 对，就是给鸡的 Love Every——每个月他们给我寄鸡零食，但也有给那些疯狂鸡迷的小趣物，比如衣服或贴纸，有点好笑。我整个儿陷进鸡这件事了，所以，对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh my God. Maybe just a tactical question, how much space do you need in your yard for chickens?
turns.zh: 我的天。也许就问个战术问题：你院子里得要多大空间给鸡？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Not that much, so we let them free-range. We have a pretty big yard, but I think their actual, so there's their little coop, and then they've got a run that's fenced in. The run is maybe like, I don't know, five feet by eight feet or something, but you can go a lot smaller. If you go to Home Depot, they actually sell pre-made coops and runs. I think if you have a decent sized backyard, they'll be fine. I've known people with pretty small yards, and you just let your chickens out and they're happy and they'll find worms in a few yards.
turns.zh: 不用太大，所以我们让它们自由放养。我们院子挺大，但我想它们实际用的——就是那个小 coop（鸡舍），然后有个 fence 围起来的 run（活动区）。那个 run 大概……我不知道，五英尺乘八英尺左右，但你可以小得多。如果你去 Home Depot，他们其实卖现成的 coop 和 run。我想只要你有个体面大小的后院，它们就没问题。我认识院子挺小的人，你就把鸡放出来，它们很开心，会在几码大的地方找虫子吃。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh man. All right. A new project to look into.
turns.zh: 哦天呐。行。一个可以研究的新项目。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Please get chickens, do it.
turns.zh: 请去养鸡，去吧。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. Maya, we've talked about chickens, dogfooding, gut level decisions, Radical Candor, so many things. Thank you so much for being here. Two final questions. Where can folks find you online if they want to reach out, and how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 好。Maya，我们聊了鸡、dogfooding、凭直觉决策、Radical Candor，好多好多。太感谢你来了。最后两个问题。大家想在网上找你、联系你，去哪儿？还有听众能怎么帮到你？

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: I'm on threads, I guess, and I'm on LinkedIn. I'm Maya Fish on most social media, and then I'm on LinkedIn, and then, what was the second one? How can people be useful to me?
turns.zh: 我在 Threads 上，我想，还有 LinkedIn。我在大部分社交媒体上叫 Maya Fish，然后我在 LinkedIn 上，然后，第二个问题是什么来着？大家怎么帮到我？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Listen to your podcast on Spotify, and then send me your feedback. I would love to know either as a podcast creator or as a podcast listener. Always happy to hear what Spotify can be doing more of or better to help you out.
turns.zh: 在 Spotify 上听你的播客，然后给我你的反馈。我想知道，不管你是作为播客创作者还是作为听众。我一直很乐意听到 Spotify 还能多做或做好什么来帮到你。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Maya, thank you so much for being here.
turns.zh: 太棒了。Maya，太感谢你来了。

turns.speaker: Maya Prohovnik
turns.en: Thank you so much.
turns.zh: 太感谢了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Bye, everyone. Thank you so much for listening. turns.zh: 拜拜，各位。非常感谢收听。如果你觉得这期有价值，可以在 Apple Podcasts、Spotify，或你最喜欢的播客 app 上订阅本节目。另外，请考虑给我们评分或留个评论，那真的能帮其他听众找到这个播客。你可以在 lennyspodcast.com 找到所有往期节目或了解更多关于本节目。下集见。
